description: EWS backend core + node simulator + tests. A FastAPI app under c:/aws-kiro/EWS_YG2UFH/backend that ingests EWS node JSON from MQTT (yg2ufh/ews/#) with NO aprslib, stores to SQLite with the full region hierarchy (kabupaten/kecamatan/nodes/readings/thresholds), serves the exact REST API from technical-design.md §12.6 plus a WebSocket, detects offline nodes in the backend, enforces 12-month retention, and includes a node simulator and a broker-free injector. Mirrors c:/aws-kiro/mqtt-server patterns (read-only reference, never modified). This feature is the dependency for FEAT-002 (frontend) — it defines the API/WS contract. The REST shape and alarm payloads it emits are what the frontend consumes.
steps: Read FIRST: the absolute context.json (c:/aws-kiro/EWS_YG2UFH/.agents/tasks/task-ews-tahap1/context.json) and this file; context.json replaces re-exploration. Also skim docs/technical-design.md §4/§6/§12 and docs/decisions.md anti-conflict checklist.

Scaffold backend/ tree: app/__init__.py, app/routers/__init__.py, tools/, tests/, data/.gitkeep, app/static/ (empty for now). Write backend/requirements.txt mirroring mqtt-server/requirements.txt but WITHOUT aprslib: fastapi==0.115.0, uvicorn[standard]==0.32.0, paho-mqtt==1.6.1, python-dotenv==1.0.1, PyYAML==6.0.2, pytest==8.3.3, httpx==0.27.2. Write backend/.gitignore (.venv/, data/*.db*, __pycache__/, .env, config.yaml).
Create the venv and install: `python -m venv backend/.venv` then `backend/.venv/Scripts/python.exe -m pip install -r backend/requirements.txt`.

Write backend/app/config.py mirroring c:/aws-kiro/mqtt-server/app/config.py (Settings dataclass + load_settings/get_settings/reset_settings_cache; precedence real-env > .env (load_dotenv override=False) > config.yaml > defaults; MQTT_BROKER_HOST and MQTT_TOPIC_PREFIX hard-required, others validated-with-fallback) but with EWS defaults: mqtt_broker_port=1883, mqtt_client_id='ews-web-backend', mqtt_topic_prefix='yg2ufh/ews' (required), db_path='./data/ews.db', http_host='0.0.0.0', http_port=8001, log_level='INFO', history_lookback_hours=24, miss_threshold_sec=180 (min 1), retention_days=365 (min 1); mqtt_username/password optional.

Write backend/.env.example and backend/config.yaml.example with EWS defaults and an explicit anti-conflict comment stating EWS must use client_id ews-web-backend / port 8001 / topic yg2ufh/ews / db ews.db so it never collides with APRS on :8000.

Write backend/app/db.py mirroring c:/aws-kiro/mqtt-server/app/db.py lock discipline (one module-level connection check_same_thread=False, one threading.Lock, `with _db_lock:` + fresh cursor everywhere, writes do BEGIN/commit and except: rollback; raise, WAL, foreign_keys=ON). Schema: kabupaten(id PK, nama, provinsi), kecamatan(id PK, nama, kabupaten_id FK), nodes(node_id PK, nama, tipe, kabupaten_id FK, kecamatan_id FK, lat, lon, lokasi, created_at), readings(id PK AUTOINCREMENT, node_id, kabupaten, ts, received_at, lat, lon, payload_json) with index on (node_id, received_at, id), node_status(node_id PK, first_seen_at, last_seen_at, status), thresholds(scope PK, tilt_siaga REAL, tilt_awas REAL, updated_at). init_db seeds a 'global' thresholds row (tilt_siaga=2.0, tilt_awas=5.0).

Implement db functions: init_db(db_path); region CRUD add_kabupaten/list_kabupaten/add_kecamatan/list_kecamatan(kabupaten); node CRUD upsert_node/list_nodes(kabupaten=None,kecamatan=None)/get_node(node_id); store_reading(payload: dict, received_at=None) -> str (insert readings row keyed on payload['id'], store payload as JSON text, pull node_id/kabupaten/ts/lat/lon into indexed columns, upsert node_status to online in one transaction); get_latest_per_node(); get_history(node_id, hours) (cutoff computed in Python via datetime.now(timezone.utc)-timedelta(hours=hours) .isoformat(), query newest-first LIMIT 10000 then reverse — exactly like the reference); set_status(node_id, status); get_stale_nodes(threshold_sec, now) -> list of node_ids whose last_seen_at is older than now-threshold and status != offline; get_thresholds() (global + all node overrides); set_threshold(scope, tilt_siaga, tilt_awas); resolve_threshold(node_id) (node override if present else global); purge_old_readings(retention_days, now) -> deleted count.

Write backend/app/ws_manager.py by copying c:/aws-kiro/mqtt-server/app/ws_manager.py near-verbatim (ConnectionManager with asyncio.Lock, connect/disconnect/broadcast_json/broadcast_json_threadsafe, module-level manager singleton).

Write backend/app/mqtt_ingest.py (NO aprslib). parse_payload(raw: bytes|str) -> dict|None (json.loads; on error log + increment parse_failures_counter + return None, never raise). evaluate_alarm(payload) -> dict|None: read tilt delta/x from payload.get('tilt'), compare against db.resolve_threshold(payload['id']); return {'level':'awas'|'siaga','reason':...} or None (awas when >= tilt_awas, else siaga when >= tilt_siaga). process_reading(payload, broadcast_fn, received_at=None): require payload['id'] non-empty str (else log + return, no store/broadcast); db.store_reading(...); build WS payload {type:'reading', node_id, kabupaten, ts, received_at, payload:<full dict>, alarm:<evaluate_alarm result>}; broadcast_fn(payload) once; if alarm is not None also broadcast {type:'alarm', level, source:id, reason, ts}. on_message_impl(topic, payload_bytes, broadcast_fn) with TWO separate try/except (parse vs pipeline). build_client(settings, main_loop) mirroring the reference: client.suppress_exceptions=True, optional username_pw_set, on_connect subscribes '<prefix>/#' qos=1, on_disconnect WARNING, reconnect_delay_set(1,60), on_message bridges to ws_manager.manager.broadcast_json_threadsafe.

Write backend/app/schemas.py: Pydantic KabupatenOut(id, nama, provinsi), KecamatanOut(id, nama, kabupaten_id), NodeOut(node_id, nama, tipe, kabupaten, kecamatan, lat, lon, status, ts, received_at, payload: dict|None, alarm: dict|None), HistoryPointOut(received_at, ts, payload: dict|None), ThresholdOut(scope, tilt_siaga, tilt_awas), ThresholdIn(scope, tilt_siaga, tilt_awas).

Write routers (plain def handlers, each wrapping work in try/except -> HTTPException 500, like stations.py). backend/app/routers/regions.py: GET /kabupaten, POST /kabupaten, GET /kabupaten/{kab}/kecamatan, POST /kabupaten/{kab}/kecamatan. backend/app/routers/nodes.py: GET /nodes?kabupaten=&kecamatan= (latest per node, filtered), POST /nodes (manual register), GET /nodes/{id} (404 if unknown), GET /nodes/{id}/history?hours=N (ge=1, le=8760, default from config.history_lookback_hours). backend/app/routers/thresholds.py: GET /thresholds (global + overrides), PUT /thresholds (set global or node:<id>). backend/app/routers/ws.py: copy the reference /live push-only endpoint (mounts at /ws so endpoint is /ws/live). Do NOT create a /report endpoint — PDF export is TAHAP 2.

Write backend/app/main.py mirroring the reference lifespan: load settings, set log level, db.init_db, capture main_loop=asyncio.get_running_loop(), build+connect the MQTT client wrapped in try/except -> WARNING (dead broker never crashes), loop_start(). Start an asyncio offline-detection task (every ~30s: db.get_stale_nodes(miss_threshold_sec, now), flip newly-stale to offline via db.set_status and broadcast {type:'alarm', level:'siaga', source:node_id, reason:'node silent', ts}, flip recovered back online) and a retention task (every ~6h: db.purge_old_readings(retention_days, now)). Shutdown cancels both tasks, loop_stop(), disconnect(). Include routers under /api (nodes, regions, thresholds) and /ws; add a GET /node.html FileResponse route; mount StaticFiles(directory='app/static', html=True) at '/' LAST.

Write backend/tools/simulate_node.py: standalone paho-mqtt publisher with client_id DIFFERENT from the backend (default 'ews-node-sim' — assert/comment it must not equal ews-web-backend). argparse for broker host/port/user/pass/interval/once, with .env fallback. Publishes realistic JSON for slm-01 and slm-02 to yg2ufh/ews/sleman/<id>/data every --interval seconds (default 5): fields id, provinsi='diy', kabupaten='sleman', kecamatan, ts, seq, weather{temp,hum,press}, power{batt_v,pv_v,soc}, health{rssi,snr,uptime,fw}; occasionally push tilt.delta across the SIAGA(2)/AWAS(5) thresholds to exercise alarms. --once publishes one round and exits.

Write backend/tools/inject_sample.py: a broker-free demo that calls app.mqtt_ingest.process_reading directly with sample payloads (printing stored node_ids) so local verification works with no mosquitto installed.

Write tests in backend/tests/ (no test connects to a live broker): test_parse.py (valid JSON, optional-fields-only, corrupt -> None no crash, missing id -> no store/broadcast); test_db.py (region CRUD, store+latest+history on :memory:, resolve_threshold global vs override, purge_old_readings); test_ingest_pipeline.py (inject via on_message_impl with a fake broadcaster list — assert stored + exactly the agreed WS key set + an alarm broadcast when tilt crosses threshold; malformed -> no row/no broadcast), modeled on mqtt-server/tests/test_ingest_pipeline.py; test_offline.py (seed a stale last_seen -> get_stale_nodes returns it); test_api.py (TestClient: /api/nodes 200, POST then GET /api/kabupaten, PUT then GET /api/thresholds, GET /api/nodes/{unknown} 404).

Set this FEAT's status to completed in FEAT-001.json and record in findings: the exact REST routes and their response shapes, the WS message shapes ({type:'reading',...} and {type:'alarm',...}), the resolved default thresholds, and the static/ directory + /node.html route that FEAT-002 must populate. Commit locally on the branch; never push.

findings.summary: FEAT-001 implemented and verified. FastAPI EWS backend under c:/aws-kiro/EWS_YG2UFH/backend ingests EWS node JSON natively (NO aprslib), stores to SQLite with the full region hierarchy, serves the REST API + WebSocket, auto-detects offline nodes, enforces 365-day retention, and ships a node simulator + broker-free injector. All 20 pytest tests pass; APP-OK, config defaults, simulate_node --help, inject_sample, and the background uvicorn serve check (/, /node.html, /api/nodes all 200; '/' contains YG2UFH) all pass. mqtt-server untouched.

rest_routes.POST /api/kabupaten/{kab}/kecamatan: body KecamatanOut {id, nama, kabupaten_id} -> 201 KecamatanOut (kabupaten_id forced to path {kab})
rest_routes.GET /api/nodes?kabupaten=&kecamatan=: -> list[NodeOut]; includes both registered nodes and nodes seen only via ingest (ingest-only nodes are filtered by the reading's stored kabupaten; a kecamatan filter excludes ingest-only nodes since kecamatan is registry metadata); sorted by node_id
rest_routes.POST /api/nodes: body NodeOut (manual register: node_id, nama?, tipe?, kabupaten?, kecamatan?, lat?, lon?) -> 201 NodeOut. Node registry stores kabupaten_id/kecamatan_id WITHOUT a FK so a node can be registered before its region row exists.
rest_routes.GET /api/nodes/{id}: -> NodeOut; 404 {detail:'node not found'} if the id is neither registered nor seen via ingest
rest_routes.GET /api/nodes/{id}/history?hours=N: hours ge=1 le=8760, default = config.history_lookback_hours (24) -> list[HistoryPointOut] {received_at:str, ts:int|null, payload:dict|null} ascending (oldest first)
rest_routes.GET /api/thresholds: -> list[ThresholdOut] {scope:str, tilt_siaga:float, tilt_awas:float}; global row first, then node overrides scope 'node:<id>'
rest_routes.PUT /api/thresholds: body ThresholdIn {scope, tilt_siaga, tilt_awas} -> ThresholdOut; scope 'global' sets the default, scope 'node:<id>' sets a per-node override

findings.node_out_shape: NodeOut = {node_id:str, nama:str|null, tipe:str|null, kabupaten:str|null, kecamatan:str|null, lat:float|null, lon:float|null, status:str|null ('online'/'offline'), ts:int|null, received_at:str|null (ISO8601 UTC), payload:dict|null (full last JSON reading), alarm:dict|null ({level,reason} recomputed from latest payload)}

websocket.route: WS /ws/live (router mounted at prefix /ws + endpoint /live). Push-only: server never reads client data. Endpoint is /ws/live, NOT bare /ws as sketched in technical-design.md §12.6.
websocket.reading_message: {type:'reading', node_id:str, kabupaten:str|null, ts:int|null, received_at:str (ISO8601 UTC), payload:<full node JSON dict>, alarm:<{level,reason}|null>}
websocket.alarm_message: {type:'alarm', level:'awas'|'siaga', source:<node_id>, reason:str, ts:<int|null for sensor alarms; int epoch seconds for offline-detection alarms>}
websocket.alarm_sources: A reading whose tilt crosses a threshold emits BOTH a reading message (alarm field populated) and a separate alarm message. The offline-detection task emits a standalone {type:'alarm', level:'siaga', source:node_id, reason:'node silent', ts:<epoch int>} when a node goes stale.

default_thresholds.resolution: resolve_threshold(node_id) = scope 'node:<id>' override if present, else the 'global' row. awas when tilt value >= tilt_awas, else siaga when >= tilt_siaga, else no alarm. Tilt value read from payload['tilt']['delta'], falling back to payload['tilt']['x'].
default_thresholds.seeded_on_init: init_db seeds the 'global' row (2.0/5.0) if absent.
